speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have experienced occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings since your tympanoplasty. To help me understand what might be going wrong, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of chronic ear infections and the specific trigger of pain while eating suggests we need to evaluate for a specific type of nerve involvement. REQUEST TEST: High-Resolution CT Temporal Bone. Can you describe exactly which movements or sensations trigger the shooting pain?

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of chronic ear infections, the timing post-tympanoplasty, and the specific triggers of pain during chewing and pressure on the cartilage strongly suggest a nerve entrapment or neuroma. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with Temporal Bone Focus. Can you tell me if you have experienced any numbness in your lower lip or chin?

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal readings and your description of pain triggered by chewing and pressure on the cartilage, following a recent tympanoplasty, are highly concerning for a recurrent neuroma or nerve entrapment. Have you noticed any changes in the sensation of your tongue or cheek on the affected side?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigeminal Neuralgia secondary to recurrent glomus tympanicum or neuroma post-tympanoplasty.
